title: GTA 6 会让互联网崩溃吗？
content:
Will Grand Theft Auto 6 break the internet? | GamesIndustry.biz

Read our editorial policy
.
Back in September 2025, the launch of Hollow Knight: Silksong
crashed the digital storefronts
of Nintendo, PlayStation, Xbox, and Steam, as players who had waited over eight years for a follow-up to 2017's Hollow Knight rushed to download the highly anticipated sequel.
The wait for a sequel to Grand Theft Auto 5 has been even longer – some 13 years – and the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6 will be orders of magnitude bigger than Silksong's.
Silksong sold
7 million units in the first three months
, reaching a peak of over
half a million concurrent players a day after launch
. GTA 6, by contrast, has
already been pre-ordered by nearly 8 million players according to Sensor Tower estimates
, with many more sales expected at launch on November 19. And whereas Silksong came in at a svelte download size of 8GB on Steam, GTA 6 weighs in at a whopping 212GB.
Hollow Knight: Silksong put stores under strain in 2025  |
Image credit:
Team Cherry
Importantly, GTA 6 is also the first AAA blockbuster of this scale to launch as a digital-only release. When GTA 5 launched back in 2013, the focus of the games business was still largely physical – but this time around, everyone who wants to buy the game will have to download it.
The pre-load period for GTA 6
starts at midnight on November 10
, ahead of the official launch on November 19. Will the PlayStation and Xbox digital storefronts hold up? And how will the internet more widely cope with the strain?
GamesIndustry.biz
asked a group of experts about what to expect.
Prior evidence
Joost van Dreunen, founder of Aldora and
author of the SuperJoost Substack
, points to the launch of Grand Theft Auto 5's online component in October 2013; it's not well remembered now, but it didn't go smoothly.
"It effectively melted Rockstar's infrastructure, which ultimately didn't hurt the franchise, but did create a massive hiccup at the time," he says. The online component for GTA 6 is still further down the line, with just the single-player version launching next week, so Rockstar doesn't have to worry about its servers just yet – that's the platform holders' concern. "The heavy lifting sits with Sony and Microsoft, not Rockstar," says van Dreunen.
"Nobody wants to be the platform that fell over on the biggest launch in a decade"
He expects the platform holders will be adding plenty of server capacity, and the lack of other game launches around GTA 6 (
aside from a gung-ho few
) will help to ease the strain, along with the option to pre-load well ahead of release. It's likely that both Sony and Microsoft are pulling all the stops out behind the scenes. "Nobody wants to be the platform that fell over on the biggest launch in a decade."
GamesIndustry.biz
contacted both PlayStation and Xbox for comment, but neither has responded. However, an old Sony hand says there's good reason for optimism.
Gordon Thornton  |
Image credit:
ZBD
Gordon Thornton spent 17 years at Sony, during which time he oversaw the development of PlayStation Network and the PlayStation Store, and he is now chief commercial officer at
ZBD
. He says that Sony is well equipped to deal with the infrastructure demands of GTA 6, having previously fallen short in the past.
"If you go back as far as the first Call of Duty map packs, we were overwhelmed and learned the hard way," Thornton explains. "My claim to fame is we took out Apple and every other digital merchant working on Worldpay at the time with the first Call of Duty map pack, because the transactions per second on our payment gateway failed. Access-wise, however, we now understand that through a very sophisticated distributed architecture."
Drip feed
Thornton says that in the years since, the option to pre-load games has eased the strain on download servers, as players can begin downloading huge files well before the day of release. And the fact that Rockstar started taking pre-orders
back in June
will no doubt help. Silksong, by contrast, only had its release date revealed
a couple of weeks before launch
, and there was no option to download the game ahead of time.
Joost van Dreunen  |
Image credit:
THIS 2023/Alexander Håkansson
"Silksong had no pre-orders, so the entire download and the entire purchase hit Steam and the console stores in the same minute, and the stores buckled," notes van Dreunen.
Thornton adds that the sheer level of excitement surrounding Silksong "likely stumped" the platforms, but says that pre-loading will help manage demand for Grand Theft Auto 6.
"Consoles load it up and download it gradually, ensuring the distribution network is not overloaded. When reaching the launch minute, it is just a key exchange, which is quick even with millions of downloads."
Simon Carless, author of the
GameDiscoverCo
newsletter, says that the pre-orders and pre-load will "significantly alleviate pressure" on PlayStation and Xbox.
"The pre-load is starting November 10, and requires up to 212 GB of local drive space, so that's very hefty," he explains. "So having an extra nine days to gradually send out the bulk of the data to players' computers is vital. There still might be a Day 1 patch/extra download, but if so, it'll be very incremental."
Pre-loading will help to smooth the launch of GTA 6  |
Image credit:
Rockstar Games
But van Dreunen warns that the real bottleneck could come on launch day, which in contrast to Silksong, could see "tens of millions day-of buyers, not a few hundred thousand."
Neil McRae, chief technology and innovation officer at UK internet provider
CityFibre
, says that although pre-loading will help to manage overall demand, "there's no getting away from the fact that launch day will be extremely busy, as many people will wait until launch to buy."
Internet infrastructure
There's also the question of what kind of pressure will be placed on the telecom infrastr
